liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Ripple** (1 review): The audience showed no reaction when the song started, suggesting few knew the music [4]

## The recordings

- **gd80-12-06.cantor.clugston.5478.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): audience recording; 9 songs; 53 min; rated 4.41/5 by 49 [1]. Said about its sound: Sound is very good with strong ambience, despite the absence of a PA system; Sound quality is just fine under the circumstances, making the listener feel present; The recording is recommended for use with expensive headphones [3][6][7][8][11][13][14]
- **gd1980-12-06.151263.betty.master.flac16**: source not stated; 9 songs; 52 min; rated 2.71/5 by 7 [2]

## Around the show

- Audience appeared to consist mainly of children in wheelchairs, possibly linked to Bridge School [3]
- Few people attended, and there was no reaction to the start of Ripple [4]
- A warm, heartfelt performance; the reviewer was the same age as Jerry when recorded [6]
- Jerry introduced the band; the audience was described as a real Betty-Audience [7]
- Jerry over-enunciates words while singing to kids, likely because few knew the music [8]
- The band played for special needs children, with a Stealie sticker on a wheelchair [9]
- The emcee thanked clowns and mispronounced Weir's name before introducing the band [10]
- A child told Jerry he wanted rock-n-roll, and Jerry responded to the request [11]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd80-12-06.cantor.clugston.5478.sbeok.shnf**: taped by Betty Cantor-Jackson; source: Audience Recording [1]. Also: Betty Cantor-Jackson's master audience cassette transferred to DAT, then CDR, and SHN'ed by Scott Clugston [1]
- **gd1980-12-06.151263.betty.master.flac16**: taped by Recording by Betty Cantor-Jackson; transferred by All transfers and mastering by Jim Blackwood  Speed Correction by Jason Chastain; source: AKG C414 Stereo Pair > Sony D5 - Betty Cantor-Jackson's Master Cassette (UD-XL II 60) [2]. Also: Master tape originally broadcast on 91.3 FM KXCI Tucson's Dead Air in the early 1990s [2]

## Art and photos

- Poster by Michael Parrish: [Mill Valley Recreation Center, December 6, 1980: Grateful Dead (Beneficial Jerry)](https://lostlivedead.blogspot.com/2025/04/mill-valley-recreation-center-december.html) [16]
- Poster by Michael Parrish: [Mill Valley Recreation Center, December 6, 1980: Grateful Dead (Beneficial Jerry)](https://lostlivedead.blogspot.com/2025/04/mill-valley-recreation-center-december.html) [17]
